hook: David Silver is a computer scientist known for leading reinforcement learning research at DeepMind. He earned his PhD at the University of Alberta under reinforcement learning pioneer Richard Sutton, then became a professor at University College London while also leading DeepMind's reinforcement learning research. He led the teams behind DeepMind's Atari-playing deep Q-network, AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, and MuZero, a series of systems that mastered Go, chess, shogi, and Atari games through self-play and learned models. He later contributed to AlphaFold's protein structure predictions and to AlphaProof, a system that reached silver-medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad. He has since stepped back from leading DeepMind's reinforcement learning team to become CEO of a new venture, Ineffable Intelligence, while remaining a professor at UCL.

standing.watch: What comes next in the records is mostly institutional. Ineffable Intelligence is described only as a new venture with Silver as CEO, and the records give no detail on its plans, funding or products. The Kadrey v. Meta Platforms case remains unresolved at the point the records reach, with the plaintiffs seeking interlocutory appeal certification and a date of 2026-08-25 attached to that step. AlphaProof's International Mathematical Olympiad result stands as the most recent research contribution the records attribute to him. Beyond those items, the records do not say what Silver's next research direction will be or how Ineffable Intelligence will relate to his DeepMind work.
standing.record: The site's records trace one arc: a PhD at the University of Alberta under reinforcement learning pioneer Richard Sutton, a professorship at University College London, and leadership of DeepMind's reinforcement learning research, with results published in Nature and Science. The named systems are the deep Q-network, AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, MuZero, AlphaFold and AlphaProof. Against that body of work the litigation record is thin, consisting of a single case on the site, Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, Inc., in which summary judgment was granted for Meta on fair use in June 2025. That entry names Meta Platforms, not Silver or Ineffable Intelligence. The pattern across the coverage is research achievement rather than legal exposure, and the records add nothing further on the case beyond the plaintiffs' bid for interlocutory appeal certification.
standing.standing: David Silver's standing in artificial intelligence rests on the reinforcement learning systems he led at DeepMind, including the Atari-playing deep Q-network, AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero and MuZero, which mastered Go, chess, shogi and Atari games through self-play and learned models. He also contributed to AlphaFold's protein structure predictions and to AlphaProof, which reached silver-medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad. He is a professor at University College London, a Fellow of the Royal Society and a Fellow of AAAI, and a recipient of the ACM Prize in Computing. He has stepped back from leading DeepMind's reinforcement learning team to become CEO of a new venture, Ineffable Intelligence, while remaining a professor at UCL. The records therefore show influence running through both the research lineage he built and the company he now heads.

achievements.title: Led AlphaGo
achievements.impact: Built the first program to defeat a professional Go player and, in 2016, the world champion Lee Sedol, a milestone many expected was a decade away.

achievements.title: Led AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero
achievements.impact: Showed that a single algorithm could master Go, chess, and shogi purely through self-play, without any human game data.

achievements.title: Led MuZero
achievements.impact: Extended self-play mastery to settings where the rules of the environment are not known in advance, unifying planning and model-based learning.

achievements.title: ACM Prize in Computing
achievements.impact: Recognized for fundamental contributions to reinforcement learning and its application to superhuman game-playing systems.
